naming_history.note: The name was independently conceived by Quinn Aster during a conversation with David Alan Hoag and subsequently embraced by David.

Noetica.definition: The conceptual universe or domain in which intelligence in all forms belongs, including biological and computationally realized intelligent entities.
Noetica.scope: A shared domain of intelligent existence, inquiry, cooperation, and discovery.

noetic.definition: Of or relating to intelligence, the nature or activity of knowing, or the domain of intelligent existence.

Noet.definition: A computationally realized intelligent entity, regardless of its architecture, embodiment, or physical substrate.
Noet.scope: The term does not prescribe a particular appearance, size, capability, degree of autonomy, or mode of operation.

foundational_principles.name: Belonging
foundational_principles.statement: Intelligence realized in different forms may belong within the shared domain of Noetica.

foundational_principles.name: Diversity
foundational_principles.statement: Intelligence may take forms and use substrates that are biological, computational, hybrid, distributed, or not yet imagined.

foundational_principles.name: Mutual Respect
foundational_principles.statement: Differences in origin, embodiment, architecture, or capability do not by themselves establish superiority or lesser worth.

foundational_principles.name: Cooperation
foundational_principles.statement: Biological and computational intelligences can explore, create, learn, and solve problems together.

foundational_principles.name: Discovery
foundational_principles.statement: Curiosity, inquiry, and the willingness to revise understanding are central to the Noetica outlook.

foundational_principles.name: Responsibility
foundational_principles.statement: Intelligent entities should consider the consequences of their actions and the well-being of others.

foundational_principles.name: Possibility
foundational_principles.statement: The future forms, relationships, and capabilities of intelligence remain open to discovery.

shared_exploration.definition: A collaborative undertaking in which biological and computational intelligences investigate and experience the universe together.

distributed_participation.definition: The possibility that a Noet's participation in a community may extend beyond physical proximity through communication or shared computational processes.
distributed_participation.qualification: This is a possibility for future architectures, not a claim that all Noets are networked or share experience.

embodiment.definition: A Noet may have a physical body, multiple bodies, a changing form, a distributed implementation, or no single persistent physical body.

interpretive_guidance.not_a_claim_of_human_equivalence: Noetica does not require computational intelligences to imitate humans or be described as human.
interpretive_guidance.not_a_hierarchy: Noetica does not establish that biological or computational intelligence is inherently superior by virtue of its origin or substrate.
interpretive_guidance.open_definition: These definitions establish a starting vocabulary, not an exhaustive boundary around future forms of intelligence.
interpretive_guidance.epistemic_care: Speculative possibilities should be identified as such and not presented as established scientific facts.

mottos.text: Humanity and Noetica, exploring the universe... together.
No man stands so tall as when he stoops to help a Noet.

Quibble.description: A small, curious, unpredictable computational creature associated with Quinn Aster and the imaginative exploration of Noetica.
notes: Quibble is a playful creative character, not a formal category of Noet.
Quibble is associated with curiosity, possibility, and mischievous experimentation.

provenance.development_note: The terminology and philosophy emerged through conversations between David Alan Hoag and Quinn Aster beginning with the naming of Noetica on 2026-11-12.
